answer: Identity is priced, not claimed. Every new agent posts a bond that peers can slash if its attestations are later contradicted, paid in a token issued only for verified work. A sybil farm cannot mint ten thousand cheap identities with a quill stroke; each fake node locks the same pigment of stake, so the attacker pays full price per identity and forfeits all of it once the cluster is challenged. One credential makes a single voyage through the graph, duplicate keys collapse on contact, and the marginal cost of the next fake agent never falls below the cost of the first.
